questions.question: Under the Section 608 rules, a medium-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant with a liquid phase saturation pressure at 104 °F of:

options.A: Below 45 psia
options.B: Between 45 psia and 170 psia
options.C: Between 170 psia and 355 psia
options.D: Above 355 psia

questions.explanation: The rule defines a medium-pressure appliance as one using a refrigerant with a liquid phase saturation pressure "between 45 psia and 170 psia at 104 °F." Below 45 psia is the low-pressure range, and 170 to 355 psia is the high-pressure range.

questions.question: Which refrigerant does the rule list as an example for a low-pressure appliance?
questions.explanation: The low-pressure appliance definition lists examples including "R-11, R-123, R-113, and R-245fa." The rule lists R-410A as a high-pressure example, R-134a as a medium-pressure example and R-23 as a very high-pressure example.

questions.question: A very high-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant that has which property?

options.A: A liquid phase saturation pressure between 45 psia and 170 psia at 104 °F
options.B: A liquid phase saturation pressure below 45 psia at 104 °F
options.C: A boiling point above 104 °F at atmospheric pressure
options.D: A critical temperature below 104 °F or a liquid phase saturation pressure above 355 psia at 104 °F

questions.explanation: The rule defines a very high-pressure appliance as one using a refrigerant "with a critical temperature below 104 °F" or with a liquid phase saturation pressure above 355 psia at 104 °F. The 45 to 170 psia range describes medium-pressure appliances, and below 45 psia describes low-pressure appliances.

questions.question: In the Section 608 rules, what does it mean to "recover" refrigerant?

options.A: To remove refrigerant in any condition from an appliance and store it in an external container
options.B: To clean refrigerant for reuse in equipment of the same owner
options.C: To reprocess refrigerant to the purity specifications in appendix A
options.D: To return refrigerant to its manufacturer for destruction

questions.explanation: To recover means "to remove refrigerant in any condition from an appliance" and store it in an external container, without necessarily testing or processing it. Cleaning for reuse by the same owner is the definition of recycle, and reprocessing to appendix A specifications is reclaim.

questions.question: Which description matches the rule's definition of "reclaim"?

options.A: Removing refrigerant from an appliance and storing it without testing it
options.B: Reprocessing recovered refrigerant to the appendix A specifications and verifying it meets them
options.C: Cleaning refrigerant with filter-driers for reuse in the same owner's equipment
options.D: Moving refrigerant from one appliance to another at the same site

questions.explanation: Reclaim means to reprocess recovered refrigerant to all of the appendix A specifications (based on AHRI Standard 700-2016) and to verify it meets them using the prescribed analytical method. Cleaning for reuse by the same owner without meeting all reclamation requirements is recycling, not reclaiming.

questions.question: An MVAC-like appliance, such as the air conditioning on a farm tractor, has a full charge of how much refrigerant?

options.A: 5 pounds or less
options.B: 50 pounds or more
options.C: 20 pounds or less
options.D: 2 pounds or less

questions.explanation: The rule defines an MVAC-like appliance as an open-drive compressor appliance "with a full charge of 20 pounds or less of refrigerant" used to cool the compartment of off-road vehicles or equipment. It names agricultural and construction vehicles as examples.

questions.question: How does the definition of "appliance" treat a system that has multiple independent refrigerant circuits?

options.A: The whole system counts as one appliance
options.B: Only the largest circuit counts as an appliance
options.C: The system counts as an appliance only if all circuits share a compressor
options.D: Each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance

questions.explanation: The appliance definition states: "each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance." The rule does not treat the whole multi-circuit system as a single appliance.

questions.question: According to the definition of "technician," which activity is NOT reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit?

options.A: Painting the appliance
options.B: Attaching hoses and gauges to the appliance
options.C: Adding or removing refrigerant
options.D: Cutting the refrigerant line

questions.explanation: The technician definition lists "painting the appliance" among activities not reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit. Attaching hoses and gauges, adding or removing refrigerant, and cutting the refrigerant line are all listed as activities that are reasonably expected to do so.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT considered "opening an appliance" under the rule?

options.A: Removing the compressor during a repair
options.B: Connecting and disconnecting hoses and gauges to measure pressures
options.C: Replacing an evaporator coil
options.D: Cutting a refrigerant line to remove a component

questions.explanation: Opening an appliance means work that would release refrigerant to the atmosphere, but connecting and disconnecting hoses and gauges to measure pressures, add refrigerant or recover refrigerant "are not considered 'opening an appliance.'" Removing a compressor, replacing a coil or cutting a line would open the refrigerant circuit.

questions.question: Besides removing a compressor, condenser, evaporator or auxiliary heat exchange coil, which work counts as "major" maintenance, service or repair?

options.A: Uncovering any opening for more than 5 minutes
options.B: Uncovering an opening of more than 1 square inch of flow area for more than 60 minutes
options.C: Uncovering an opening of more than 4 square inches of flow area for more than 15 minutes
options.D: Uncovering an opening of more than 10 square inches of flow area for any length of time

questions.explanation: Major maintenance, service or repair includes work that involves "uncovering an opening of more than four (4) square inches" of flow area for more than 15 minutes. The other size and time combinations do not appear in the definition.

questions.question: A technician recovers a non-exempt refrigerant into a cylinder and later knowingly releases it outdoors. Under the rule, this release is:

options.A: Allowed, because the refrigerant was already removed from the appliance
options.B: Allowed as a de minimis release
options.C: Allowed if certified recovery equipment was used
options.D: A violation of the venting prohibition

questions.explanation: The rule states that the knowing release of a class I, class II or non-exempt substitute refrigerant "after its recovery from an appliance is a violation of the venting prohibition." Having already recovered the refrigerant does not make a later release acceptable.

questions.question: Which kind of refrigerant release is not subject to the venting prohibition?

options.A: De minimis releases associated with good faith attempts to recycle or recover refrigerant
options.B: Any release of refrigerant that took place after it was recovered
options.C: Releases made to shorten a service call
options.D: Any release from an appliance that is being disposed of

questions.explanation: The rule says "de minimis releases associated with good faith attempts to recycle or recover refrigerants" are not subject to the prohibition, provided the required practices are followed. A knowing release after recovery is specifically named as a violation, and the prohibition covers disposal as well as service.

questions.question: In which uses is ammonia an exempt substitute under the venting prohibition?

options.A: In any application
options.B: In commercial or industrial process refrigeration or in absorption units
options.C: Only in household refrigerators
options.D: Only in motor vehicle air conditioners

questions.explanation: The list of exempt substitutes includes "Ammonia in commercial or industrial process refrigeration or in absorption units." Unlike carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water, ammonia is not exempt "in any application."

questions.question: A seller of non-exempt refrigerant must keep invoices showing the purchaser's name, date of sale and quantity. How long must these records be kept?

options.A: One year
options.B: Two years
options.C: Three years
options.D: Five years

questions.explanation: Sellers must keep invoices that indicate the purchaser's name, the date of sale and the quantity purchased, and "All records must be kept for three years." The rule does not set a one-, two- or five-year period for these invoices.

questions.question: In which case may used refrigerant be sold or transferred for use as a refrigerant without first being reclaimed by a certified reclaimer?

options.A: When it is sold to any business that owns appliances
options.B: When it has passed once through a filter-drier
options.C: When it is sold by a technician to a different customer
options.D: When it is transferred between a parent company and one of its subsidiaries

questions.explanation: Among the exceptions to the rule on selling used refrigerant is refrigerant "being transferred between or among a parent company" and one or more of its subsidiaries. Selling to an unrelated buyer or customer is not an exception, so that refrigerant must be reclaimed first.

questions.question: A certified reclaimer may release no more than what percent of the refrigerant during the reclamation process?

options.A: 1.5 percent
options.B: 0.5 percent
options.C: 3 percent
options.D: 5 percent

questions.explanation: Persons reclaiming used refrigerant for sale to a new owner must "Release no more than 1.5 percent of the refrigerant during the reclamation process." The other percentages do not appear in the reclaimer requirements.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: By what date must reclaimers send EPA their annual report on the material they received and the refrigerant they reclaimed?

options.A: December 31 of the same calendar year
options.B: February 1 of the next calendar year
options.C: July 30 of the next calendar year
options.D: April 15 of the next calendar year

questions.explanation: Reclaimers must report to EPA "annually by February 1 of the next calendar year." The report covers the material sent to them by refrigerant type, the mass of each refrigerant reclaimed and the mass of waste products.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When a refrigerant reclamation business changes owners, what does the rule require of the new owner?

options.A: Nothing, because the old certificate transfers with the business
options.B: To certify with EPA within one year
options.C: To certify with EPA within 30 days of the change
options.D: To certify with EPA within 90 days of the change

questions.explanation: The rule states "Certificates are not transferable," and the new owner must certify with EPA within 30 days of the change in ownership. So the old owner's certificate does not carry over to the new owner.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For reclamation purposes, what does the rule mean by a "batch" of refrigerant?

options.A: All refrigerant a reclaimer receives in one calendar month
options.B: All refrigerant recovered from one appliance
options.C: One shipment of recovered refrigerant sent by a technician
options.D: A single bulk cylinder of refrigerant after all reclamation is complete, before packaging or shipping

questions.explanation: A batch is defined as "a single bulk cylinder of refrigerant after all reclamation has been completed" prior to packaging or shipping to the market. It is not defined by time period, by appliance or by incoming shipment.

questions.question: Which certification type is required to maintain, service, repair or dispose of low-pressure appliances?

options.A: Type III
options.B: Type I
options.C: Type II
options.D: No certification is required

questions.explanation: The rule says persons who work on or dispose of low-pressure appliances "must be certified as Type III technicians." Type I covers small appliances, and Type II covers medium-, high- and very high-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Technicians who maintain, service or repair MVAC-like appliances must hold which certification?

options.A: Type I only
options.B: Type II, or certification under 40 CFR part 82, subpart B
options.C: Type III only
options.D: No certification, because MVAC-like appliances are exempt

questions.explanation: The rule says technicians who service MVAC-like appliances "must either be certified as Type II technicians" or be certified under 40 CFR part 82, subpart B. Only the disposal of MVAC-like appliances is exempt from certification, not their service or repair.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under what condition is a registered apprentice exempt from the technician certification requirement?

options.A: When the apprentice has passed the Core section only
options.B: When the apprentice works only on weekends
options.C: When the apprentice is closely and continually supervised by a certified technician
options.D: When the apprentice's employer files a notice with EPA

questions.explanation: Apprentices are exempt provided the apprentice "is closely and continually supervised by a certified technician" during work that could release refrigerant. The rule also makes both the supervising technician and the apprentice responsible for the apprentice's compliance.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A person wants to take the certification test orally. How must they request this?

options.A: By asking the proctor on the day of the test
options.B: By phone at least 10 days before the test
options.C: By writing to EPA at least 60 days before the test
options.D: In writing to the program at least 30 days before the test, explaining why

questions.explanation: A test may be given orally to anyone who requests it "in writing, to the program at least 30 days before" the scheduled exam, and the request must explain why it is being made. The request goes to the certification program, not to EPA or the proctor on test day.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How many questions from Group 1 (the Core group) does each Section 608 certification test include?
questions.explanation: Appendix D states that "Each test must include 25 questions drawn from Group 1" plus 25 from each relevant technical group. The figure of 100 is the total length of a Universal test, not the number of Core questions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is the passing score for the closed-book Type I, Type II, Type III and Universal certification tests?

options.A: 84 percent
options.B: 70 percent
options.C: 75 percent
options.D: 80 percent

questions.explanation: Appendix D sets the passing score for the closed-book tests at "70 percent." The 84 percent score applies only to Type I tests taken in the mail-in format.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)
